sources.name: English Wiktionary sense-aligned translation tables via Kaikki/Wiktextract
sources.attribution: Wiktionary contributors; extracted by Wiktextract/Kaikki (Tatu Ylonen and contributors). Subset extraction, standard-language filtering, equivalent selection and English sense labels by Jenechka Cards.
sources.methodology: A concept retains one explicit English POS/etymology/translation-table meaning. Both entry-level and nested sense-level translations are read. Selection uses existing English source headword inventories (CEFR-J and the supplemental levels.json) or exact target-language top-1000 native token matches; it does not assign CEFR or transfer frequency ranks. Foreign forms are literal source translations in that exact table. Standard-language/register filters reject unknown tags, dialects, malformed annotations and unexpected script. Equivalent selection within one table prefers unqualified standard forms, then the equivalent's own-language original corpus rank, then source order. Selected tags and other eligible variants remain in the source artifact. English study sides include the exact translation heading to distinguish senses. Categories use topics of explicit parent source senses (categoryAssociation=source-parent-sense), or an exact translation heading-to-gloss/sense-id match (exact-gloss-or-sense-id); otherwise they are unassigned. Parent-sense associations are Kaikki postprocessing, not a new human disambiguation claim. Existing hand-reviewed sense keys are omitted. The shared English source POS is not independently verified as the grammatical class of every translation. No SMARTool links are inferred. Automatically extracted dictionary data, not native-speaker reviewed.
sources.sourceOrder: bulkLine is the original 1-based JSONL record number. sourceSenseOrder is the 0-based first encounter of eligible explicit translation headings, reading entry-level translations then nested senses in original array order. This is source encounter order, not a frequency ranking of meanings.
